components.css: .ds-project-story { padding: clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 5.5rem) 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.35fr) minmax(260px, 0.65fr); gap: clamp(2rem, 6vw, 7rem); align-items: center; color: var(--paper); border-block: 1px solid var(--line); text-decoration: none; } .ds-project-cover { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 1200 / 630; display: grid; place-items: center; overflow: hidden; color: var(--signal); background-color: var(--ink-raised); background-image: linear-gradient(var(--line) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, var(--line) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 44px 44px; transition: transform 800ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-project-cover::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 18%; border: 1px solid var(--signal); } .ds-project-cover i { z-index: 1; padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; background: var(--ink); font: 400 0.72rem/1.5 var(--mono); letter-spacing: 0.04em; font-style: normal; } .ds-project-copy { display: block; } .ds-project-copy small { color: var(--signal); font: 400 0.72rem/1.5 var(--mono); letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-project-copy strong { margin: 1.2rem 0; display: block; font: 500 clamp(2.15rem, 4vw, 4.5rem)/1 var(--display); letter-spacing: -0.035em; } .ds-project-copy p { margin: 0; color: var(--paper-muted); font: 400 1rem/1.65 var(--sans); } .ds-project-copy b { width: max-content; margin-top: 2rem; padding-bottom: 0.35rem; display: block; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-strong); font: 500 0.78rem/1.4 var(--sans); } .ds-project-story:hover .ds-project-cover { transform: scale(1.015); } .ds-project-story:hover .ds-project-copy b { color: var(--signal); border-color: var(--signal); } .ds-project-story:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset: 5px; } .ds-project-story:active .ds-project-cover { transform: scale(1); }

components.name: Motion Control
components.description: A persistent compact control that makes the page’s motion state explicit and reversible.
components.css: .ds-motion-control { min-height: 40px; padding: 0 0.85rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.65rem; color: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--line-strong); border-radius: 10px; background: rgba(8, 10, 9, 0.92); font: 400 0.7rem/1 var(--mono); letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-motion-control strong { color: var(--signal); font-weight: 500; } .ds-motion-bars { display: flex; gap: 3px; align-items: center; } .ds-motion-bars i { width: 2px; height: 10px; display: block; background: var(--paper); } .ds-motion-bars i:last-child { height: 4px; transition: height 180ms ease-out; } .ds-motion-control:hover { border-color: var(--signal); } .ds-motion-control:hover .ds-motion-bars i:last-child { height: 10px; } .ds-motion-control:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset: 5px; } .ds-motion-control:active { color: var(--signal); }

narrative.overview:
This system behaves like an independent engineering journal: human presence leads, disciplined typography establishes authority, and technical detail appears as annotation rather than decoration. The portrait and oversized editorial serif provide the emotional entry point; concise claims, ruled modules, and measurable outcomes convert that attention into credible proof.

The atmosphere is dark, calm, and precise, with generous negative space and a restrained density that lets each proof point land. Warm ivory sections create deliberate chapter breaks, while signal green marks state, emphasis, and evidence. The system refuses generic developer-dashboard chrome, terminal cosplay, promotional gloss, and ornamental effects that compete with the work.
keyCharacteristics: Portrait-led editorial storytelling with technical annotations.
A disciplined charcoal, warm ivory, and signal-green palette.
Oversized serif statements balanced by plain sans-serif explanation.
Proof-first modules structured by rules, grids, and measurable outcomes.
Purposeful focus-rack motion with a persistent motion-off control.

rules.name: The Signal Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use signal green for state, selection, proof, or a single editorial emphasis—not as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Paper Chapter Rule
rules.body: Warm-ivory surfaces mark a real narrative change; they do not appear as scattered cards inside the charcoal world.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif tells the human story, sans-serif explains, and mono labels evidence; do not swap their jobs for novelty.

rules.name: The One Editorial Gesture Rule
rules.body: A heading may use one italic or signal-green phrase, but never multiple competing treatments.

rules.name: The Grid Is a Quiet Instrument Rule
rules.body: Align portrait edges, rules, labels, and text blocks to the shared grid; the grid may be visible as a faint guide in the hero but must not become decoration elsewhere.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Never add wide ambient shadows to cards or controls; use tonal contrast, a ruled edge, or a state change to establish hierarchy.

rules.name: The Focus-Rack Rule
rules.body: Motion may sharpen content from soft blur and slight vertical offset, but it must preserve readable content before JavaScript, offer a motion-off control, and collapse under reduced-motion preferences.

rules.name: The Rounded-Is-Interactive Rule
rules.body: Rounded corners signal a control or floating frame; content modules remain square and aligned to the editorial grid.

dos: Do lead with human presence, then make measurable outcomes and system evidence easy to scan.
Do use signal green sparingly for active state, verified proof, focus, or one editorial emphasis.
Do use ruled rows, chapter-level color inversions, and generous space to create hierarchy without shadows.
Do preserve readable content without JavaScript and respect both the visible motion control and prefers-reduced-motion.
Do keep serif, sans-serif, and mono type in their assigned narrative, explanatory, and annotative roles.
donts: Don't turn the interface into a generic dashboard, terminal simulation, or grid of interchangeable rounded cards.
Don't scatter signal green across decorative backgrounds, gradients, or multiple competing accents in one view.
Don't add wide drop shadows, glassy glow, or ornamental depth where a tonal shift or ruled edge is sufficient.
Don't use warm ivory as an isolated card color; reserve it for meaningful chapter changes and interaction inversions.
Don't let motion delay access to content, obscure focus, or survive a reduced-motion preference.
